subject: ventures/ci-minutes-pricing-calculator
professional: a platform/DevOps engineering lead who budgets CI spend and is choosing or leaving a hosted CI vendor; first checks: are the per-minute rates and included allowances current at each vendor's pricing page, are mandatory seat/platform fees counted, does the arithmetic (overage, 12-month projection, crossover volume) recompute, and does the --budget gate exit non-zero only when over budget

evidence.correctness: Arithmetic recomputes exactly; the rate card does not. My own script (scratchpad ci-minutes/indep.mjs, does not import engine.mjs) on the product's own rate table: 12,000 min/month gives GitLab 49, CircleCI 69, GitHub 80, Bitbucket 98, Buildkite 156 (CLI `compare --minutes 12000 --growth 6`: identical); 12-month spend at 6%/month 1,172.40 / 1,178.63 / 1,427.52 / 1,760.40 / 2,631.73 (identical); an exhaustive integer scan 0..200,000 of the cheapest provider gives switch points 3,001 (GitHub), 5,625/5,626 (GitLab), 16,999-17,002 (CircleCI), matching `crossover` (3001-5624 GitHub, 5625-16998 GitLab, 16999+ CircleCI) apart from one-minute exact-tie points labelled with the next winner. Hand: GitHub = GitLab when 8(v-2000)/1000 = 29, v = 5,625; GitLab = CircleCI above 10k when 29+10(x-10) = 15+6(x-3), x = 17 (thousand). The vendor pages themselves (docs.github.com, circleci.com, about.gitlab.com, atlassian.com, buildkite.com, github.blog, resources.github.com) could NOT be fetched: the session proxy blocks every one (curl CONNECT 403, WebFetch ENOTFOUND). Web-search result summaries citing those pages report: GitHub cut hosted runner prices from 2026-01-01 with Linux 2-core at $0.006/min (engine: $0.008); Buildkite Linux hosted agents moved to $0.004/vCPU-min (Small 2 vCPU = $0.008/min, engine $0.013) and the Pro plan's $30 per active user is mandatory (engine counts no fee); Bitbucket Standard $3.65/user (engine $3); CircleCI (free and Performance 30,000 credits = 3,000 medium minutes, $15, 10 credits/min at $0.0006) and GitLab (Premium $29, 10,000 min, $10/1,000, Free 400) agree with the engine. Rerunning my scan with those 2026 figures moves the winner above about 14,750 min/month from CircleCI to GitHub, and at 150,000 min the tool shows GitHub at $1,184 against about $888. GitLab Free namespaces can buy compute-minute packs without Premium, so 401-~3,000 minutes on GitLab costs $10/1,000 rather than the $29 Premium the engine forces. Capped at 2: arithmetic is right, the numbers a user would act on at scale are not, on secondary (search-snippet) evidence because the primary pages were unreachable.
evidence.completeness: Every README/page feature runs end to end: `compare` text and --json, --growth/--months projection, --provider and --budget gate (exit 1 over, 0 under, checked at 150,000 github budget 50 and 1,000 budget 50), --prices override merged over defaults (test and my run), `crossover` and --max, `providers` listing; page (Playwright, served locally) renders the comparison, 12-month column, crossover table and editable rate cards, example and Clear buttons work, opt-out button present, how-to page linked both ways, sitemap and llms.txt present, served copy clean (served-copy.mjs: no placeholder or retired origin). Page rate-card editing is limited to the first plan (disclosed on the page). No stubs or TODOs.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the subject: 26 tests, 26 pass, ~430 ms. Tests pin free-allowance boundaries, overage, sort order, projection path, segment contiguity, a custom-table crossover, budget gating and CLI exit codes. Seeded 7 mutants with quality_mutate.py: 4 caught (free `<=` -> `<`, growth /100 -> /1000, projection month start 0 -> 1, overage from plan.minutes -> freeMinutes), 3 survived: budget gate `>` -> `>=` (a CI job exactly at budget would fail), annual = monthly x 12 -> x 11 (the per-year column is never asserted), and the crossover grid step 1.03 -> 1.5 (equivalent on the default table, but no test would notice a skipped short segment). No test exercises the browser render() path, input validation of --prices contents, or rate-card currency.
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs (105 lines), cli.mjs (77), index.html script, all three main test files. One shared pure engine for CLI and page; small and readable. Defects found by running: (1) `--prices` with a malformed plan (`{"github":{"plans":5}}`) throws a TypeError and exits 1, the same code the README reserves for over-budget, so a CI gate reads a bad config as a budget breach; (2) negative rates are accepted (`overagePer1k: -8` prints GitHub at -$24.00/mo); (3) unknown flags are silently ignored (`--grwoth 50` exits 0 with 0% growth); (4) page: after a good run, a blank or -5000 volume shows the error line but leaves the previous report visible (index.html:139 returns before hiding #report-card); a negative growth is clamped to 0 silently ('Volume grows from 12,000 to 12,000'); (5) the footer disclaimer was copied from the email-API sibling ('each vendor's own definition of a billable email'); (6) cheapestSegments starts its grid at 100, so the 0-50 tie omits Bitbucket and Buildkite-at-0. Phone width fine (scrollWidth 375 at 375 px); no console errors.
evidence.claims: Checked 8 claims. Backed: 'nothing is uploaded' (Playwright request log: only same-origin requests; no fetch/beacon in source); DNT/GPC and local-only usage counting (usage.mjs, opt-out button); no-warranty and not-affiliated text on both pages; '10,000 Linux minutes ... differ by more than four times' (engine: 29 vs 130 = 4.5x); exit codes 0/1/2 (except the malformed --prices crash); served llms.txt URLs rewritten to marisstella.app. Not backed or misleading: (1) 'approximate public list prices as best known in 2025' (engine.mjs:12, index.html:102 and FAQ schema) is a year, not a dated per-vendor citation, and at least GitHub (2026-01-01) and Buildkite (2026) changed after it, so the page presents stale rates as current packaging; (2) the footer says the tool ignores 'deliverability and each vendor's own definition of a billable email' - wrong product; (3) the label 'Buildkite hosted agents' implies the full Buildkite charge while the mandatory per-user platform fee is not counted (the 'extra seats' caveat does not cover a fee that applies to the first user).
evidence.fitness: Walked the job of a DevOps lead with a 10-person team at 12,000 Linux minutes/month: the tool says GitLab at $49/month, but GitLab Premium is per seat ($290 for 10) and the tool's '1 seat' framing makes per-seat vendors look cheapest; CircleCI Performance includes 5 users, Bitbucket and Buildkite charge per user - none of this can be entered on the page except by hand-folding seats into 'First paid plan' price. The CLI --prices file can model it, so a careful user can get a usable number after re-entering every rate from vendor pages - which is the job the tool was meant to save. The budget gate in CI works for the per-minute line.
evidence.domain: Compared against how a platform lead prices CI: per-runner-minute rate x billable minutes + mandatory platform/seat fees + included allowances, per plan tier. The engine's model (free allowance, one plan fee with included minutes, overage per 1,000) is a reasonable skeleton and supports multiple plans, but: seats are fixed at 1 for GitLab and Bitbucket and ignored for CircleCI and Buildkite; Buildkite's mandatory platform fee is omitted; GitLab Free's pay-per-pack minutes are not offered as a plan; the free allowance and the first plan's included minutes are separate fields, so raising GitHub's free minutes to 3,000 (Pro/Team) without also editing the plan bills 3,001 minutes at $8.01 instead of $0.01 (page, Playwright); macOS/Windows multipliers and runner sizes are out of scope (disclosed). The result is a per-minute-line comparison that a practitioner would not sign off as a vendor choice without redoing it.

defects.what: Rate card is stale against 2026 vendor pricing (per web-search summaries of the vendor pages; the pages themselves were unreachable from this session): GitHub Linux 2-core $0.008 vs $0.006/min since 2026-01-01, Buildkite Linux small $0.013 vs $0.008/min, Bitbucket Standard $3 vs $3.65/user. With the 2026 figures GitHub, not CircleCI, is cheapest above about 14,750 min/month, and at 150,000 min GitHub shows $1,184 vs about $888. Dated only 'as best known in 2025', no per-vendor as-of date

Buildkite's mandatory Pro platform fee ($30 per active user, which includes 4,000 Linux vCPU-minutes) is not counted, so the 'Buildkite hosted agents' row is neither the full charge nor the right per-minute rate

Seats fixed at 1 for GitLab and Bitbucket and ignored for CircleCI/Buildkite, with no seat input on the page; per-seat vendors look cheapest (GitLab $49 at 12,000 min is $310+ for a 10-person team). GitLab Free's pay-per-pack minutes ($10/1,000 without Premium) are not offered as a plan, so 401-3,000 minutes on GitLab is priced at $29

Free allowance and first plan's included minutes are separate fields, so editing GitHub 'Free up to' to 3,000 (Pro/Team) bills 3,001 minutes at $8.01 instead of $0.01: overage counts from plan.minutes even when freeMinutes is higher

Malformed --prices content (e.g. plans not an array) throws a TypeError and exits 1, the code documented for over-budget, so a CI budget gate reads a broken config as a budget breach; negative rates are accepted and print negative costs
Tests miss the budget boundary (> -> >= survives, a job exactly at budget would fail CI) and never assert the per-year column (x12 -> x11 survives) or the crossover grid density
Page leaves the previous report visible after a blank, zero or negative volume (only a status line changes)
Footer disclaimer copied from the email-API sibling: 'ignores ... deliverability and each vendor's own definition of a billable email'
Unknown CLI flags are silently ignored (`--grwoth 50` runs at 0% growth, exit 0); page silently clamps negative growth to 0
cheapestSegments starts its grid at 100 minutes, so the first tie segment (0-400) omits Bitbucket (free to 50) and exact-tie minutes are labelled with the next winner

verdict: A small, clean CI-minutes comparator whose arithmetic is exactly right: monthly costs, the 12-month compound projection and the crossover volumes all match an independent script and an exhaustive integer scan. It misses the bar on correctness, claims and verification. The rate card is dated only 'as best known in 2025' and, by web-search summaries of the vendor pages (the pages themselves were blocked from this session), GitHub ($0.006 from 2026-01-01), Buildkite ($0.008/min plus a mandatory $30/user fee) and Bitbucket ($3.65/user) have moved, which flips the high-volume winner from CircleCI to GitHub. Seats are fixed at one, GitLab Free's pay-per-pack minutes are missing, editing a free allowance on the page mis-bills, a malformed --prices file exits with the over-budget code, the footer talks about billable email, and 3 of 7 seeded bugs survive the tests. Finished for what it claims; not yet something a platform lead would budget from.
